cemc-cayley-2007-02.title: Factor
cemc-cayley-2007-02.body:
Every term on the bottom is double a term on top: $14+42=2(7+21)$. So the fraction is $\frac12$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{1}{2}$**

cemc-cayley-2007-03.title: Simplify both sides
cemc-cayley-2007-03.body:
The left side is $2x$ and the right side is $2$, so $2x=2$ and $x=1$.

**Answer: (B) 1**

cemc-cayley-2007-06.title: Substitute
cemc-cayley-2007-06.body:
The values are $\frac25$, $\frac52=2.5$, $-3$, $3$ and $1$. The greatest is $3$.

**Answer: (D) $b-a$**

cemc-cayley-2007-08.title: Equal angles give equal sides
cemc-cayley-2007-08.body:
In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC=\angle BAC=y^\circ$, so $AC=BC$. In $\triangle CBD$, $\angle CBD=\angle CDB=x^\circ$, so $CD=BC$.

Perimeter of $\triangle CBD$: $7+2\,BC=19$, so $BC=6$. Perimeter of $\triangle ABC$: $AB+6+6=20$, so $AB=8$.

**Answer: (D) 8**

cemc-cayley-2007-09.title: Trapezoid
cemc-cayley-2007-09.body:
$AB=4+4=8$, so $BC=40\div8=5$. $MBCN$ is a trapezoid with parallel sides $MB=4$ and $NC=2$ and height $5$: area $\frac12(4+2)(5)=15$.

**Answer: (A) 15**

cemc-cayley-2007-09.title: Rectangle plus triangle
cemc-cayley-2007-09.body:
With $BC=5$, drop a vertical line from $N$ to $AB$. It cuts $MBCN$ into a $2\times5$ rectangle (area $10$) and a right triangle with legs $2$ and $5$ (area $5$). Total $15$.

**Answer: (A) 15**

cemc-cayley-2007-10.title: Work backwards
cemc-cayley-2007-10.body:
Undo each step: subtract 4, then halve. From $52$: $48\div2=24$ (second term). From $24$: $20\div2=10$ (first term).

**Answer: (D) 10**

cemc-cayley-2007-11.title: Use a variable
cemc-cayley-2007-11.body:
Say Monday was $x$ km. Then Tuesday $2x$, Wednesday $x$, Thursday $\frac12x$, Friday $x$. The shortest is Thursday: $\frac12x=5$, so $x=10$. Total: $10+20+10+5+10=55$ km.

**Answer: (A) 55 km**

cemc-cayley-2007-11.title: Start from the shortest day
cemc-cayley-2007-11.body:
Thursday is the shortest, $5$ km. Friday is double: $10$. Wednesday is double Thursday: $10$. Tuesday is double Wednesday: $20$, and Monday is half of Tuesday: $10$. Total $55$ km.

**Answer: (A) 55 km**

cemc-cayley-2007-12.title: Reflect one step at a time
cemc-cayley-2007-12.body:
$(0,0)$ is $1$ unit left of $x=1$, so its image is $1$ unit right: $(2,0)$. That point is $2$ units below $y=2$, so its image is $2$ units above: $(2,4)$.

**Answer: (E) $(2,4)$**

cemc-cayley-2007-13.title: Similar triangles
cemc-cayley-2007-13.body:
$AN:AC=AP:AB=1:2$ and the angle at $A$ is shared, so $\triangle APN\sim\triangle ABC$ with ratio $1:2$. Areas scale by $1:4$, so the area of $\triangle ABC$ is $4\times2=8$ cm².

**Answer: (A) 8 cm²**

cemc-cayley-2007-13.title: Four equal pieces
cemc-cayley-2007-13.body:
Join $C$ to $P$. The diagonal $CP$ splits rectangle $NPMC$ into two equal triangles. $\triangle PNA$ and $\triangle PNC$ have equal bases $AN=NC$ and the same height $PN$, so they have equal area; likewise $\triangle PMC$ and $\triangle PMB$. So all four small triangles have area $2$, and $\triangle ABC$ has area $8$ cm².

**Answer: (A) 8 cm²**

cemc-cayley-2007-14.title: Common denominator
cemc-cayley-2007-14.body:
$\frac{3}{x-3}=\frac{6}{2x-6}$, so the left side is $\frac{11}{2x-6}$. Then $\frac{11}{2x-6}=\frac{11}{2}$ gives $2x-6=2$.

**Answer: (A) 2**

cemc-cayley-2007-14.title: Substitute
cemc-cayley-2007-14.body:
Let $u=2x-6$, so $x-3=\frac u2$ and $\frac{3}{x-3}=\frac6u$. The equation is $\frac6u+\frac5u=\frac{11}{2}$, so $u=2$.

**Answer: (A) 2**

cemc-cayley-2007-15.title: Angle chase
cemc-cayley-2007-15.body:
All angles of the equilateral triangles are $60^\circ$. On the straight line at $B$: $\angle YBP=180^\circ-65^\circ-60^\circ=55^\circ$. At $P$: $\angle YPB=180^\circ-75^\circ-60^\circ=45^\circ$. In $\triangle BYP$: $\angle BYP=180^\circ-55^\circ-45^\circ=80^\circ$, and $\angle XYC=\angle BYP=80^\circ$ (vertically opposite). In $\triangle CXY$, $\angle XCY=60^\circ$, so $\angle CXY=180^\circ-60^\circ-80^\circ=40^\circ$.

**Answer: (C) 40°**

cemc-cayley-2007-16.title: Count each group
cemc-cayley-2007-16.body:
Arts: $6000$ students; Science: $4000$. Male Science students: $0.4\times4000=1600$. There are $5000$ males in total, so $3400$ males are in Arts, and $6000-3400=2600$ Arts students are female. $\frac{2600}{6000}\approx43.3\%$.

**Answer: (E) 43%**

cemc-cayley-2007-16.title: Count females directly
cemc-cayley-2007-16.body:
Female Science students: $60\%$ of $4000=2400$. Females total $5000$, so female Arts students are $5000-2400=2600$, i.e. $\frac{2600}{6000}\approx43\%$ of Arts.

**Answer: (E) 43%**

cemc-cayley-2007-17.title: Heroes and Villains alternate
cemc-cayley-2007-17.body:
Everyone says “Hero” to the first question no matter what (Heroes tell the truth, Villains lie), so it gives no information.

A Hero saying “Villain” about the right neighbour means that neighbour is a Villain. A Villain saying “Villain” is lying, so his right neighbour is a Hero. So types alternate around the table: $2$ Heroes and $2$ Villains (and this arrangement does give the stated answers).

**Answer: (C) 2**

cemc-cayley-2007-18.title: Equation in the total
cemc-cayley-2007-18.body:
Let there be $x$ balls. Green: $x-\frac13x-\frac27x=\frac{8}{21}x$. Also green $=2\cdot\frac27x-8=\frac{12}{21}x-8$. So $\frac4{21}x=8$, $x=42$, and green $=\frac{8}{21}\cdot42=16$.

**Answer: (B) 16**

cemc-cayley-2007-18.title: Try a convenient total
cemc-cayley-2007-18.body:
The total must be a multiple of $21$. With $21$ balls: $7$ red, $6$ blue, $8$ green, but $2\cdot6-8=4\ne8$. With $42$ balls: $14$ red, $12$ blue, $16$ green, and $2\cdot12-8=16$ ✓.

**Answer: (B) 16**

cemc-cayley-2007-19.title: Box and subtract
cemc-cayley-2007-19.body:
Enclose $ABCD$ in the rectangle with corners $(0,0)$ and $(5,3)$, area $15$. Cut off four right triangles: at the top-left legs $1,2$ (area $1$), top-right legs $4,1$ (area $2$), bottom-right legs $1,2$ (area $1$), bottom-left legs $4,1$ (area $2$). Area $=15-6=9$.

**Answer: (A) 9**

cemc-cayley-2007-20.title: Same exponent on both sides
cemc-cayley-2007-20.body:
Divide by $3$: $n^{2007}<3^{4014}=(3^2)^{2007}=9^{2007}$. Since $2007$ is odd, this means $n<9$, so the largest integer is $8$.

**Answer: (D) 8**

cemc-cayley-2007-21.title: Deduce the opponents
cemc-cayley-2007-21.body:
$T$ has played all $5$ others. So $P$'s only match was against $T$. $S$ played $4$ matches but not $P$, so $S$ played $Q,R,T,W$. Then $Q$'s two matches were $T$ and $S$. $R$ played $T$ and $S$ and not $P$ or $Q$, so its third match was $W$. Hence $W$ played $T$, $S$, $R$: $3$ matches.

**Answer: (C) 3**

cemc-cayley-2007-21.title: Pair up teams
cemc-cayley-2007-21.body:
Each match is counted twice in the total of games played, so $1+2+3+4+5+w$ is even, i.e. $w$ is odd. $T$ and $S$ played $W$ (as shown above, $S$ played everyone but $P$), so $w\ge2$, so $w\in\{3,5\}$. $W$ did not play $P$ (whose only game was $T$) or $Q$ (whose two games were $T,S$), so $w\le3$. Thus $w=3$.

**Answer: (C) 3**

cemc-cayley-2007-22.title: Divisors of 12
cemc-cayley-2007-22.body:
The list is $n,n+3,n+6,n+9,n+12$. We need $n\mid n+12$, i.e. $n\mid12$. So $n\in\{1,2,3,4,6,12\}$: $6$ lists.

**Answer: (D) 6**

cemc-cayley-2007-23.title: Twice the region AEHCB
cemc-cayley-2007-23.body:
Both rectangles have area $216$ and share the unshaded region $AEHD$, so the two shaded regions have equal area; the total is $2\times$ area of $AEHCB$.

Draw a horizontal line through $E$ meeting $AB$ at $X$ and $HC$ at $Y$. In right $\triangle AXE$, $AE=12$ and $\angle XAE=30^\circ$, so $EX=6$, $AX=6\sqrt3$, area $18\sqrt3$. Rectangle $XBCY$: $(12-6\sqrt3)\cdot18=216-108\sqrt3$. In $\triangle EYH$: $EY=18-6=12$ and $\angle HEY=30^\circ$ (since $\angle AEX=60^\circ$ and $\angle AEH=90^\circ$), so $HY=\frac{12}{\sqrt3}=4\sqrt3$, area $24\sqrt3$.

Area of $AEHCB=216-66\sqrt3$, so the total shaded area is $432-132\sqrt3\approx203.37$.

**Answer: (C) 203.4**

cemc-cayley-2007-23.title: Subtract the overlap
cemc-cayley-2007-23.body:
Total shaded $=2(216-[AEHD])$. Split the overlap $AEHD$ by the segment $AH$ into right triangles $AEH$ (right angle at $E$) and $ADH$ (right angle at $D$). Use coordinates $B=(0,0)$, $A=(0,12)$, $C=(18,0)$, $D=(18,12)$. Then $E=(6,12-6\sqrt3)$ and side $EF$ has direction $(\cos30^\circ,\sin30^\circ)$; it meets $DC$ (the line $x=18$) after travelling $\frac{12}{\cos30^\circ}=8\sqrt3$, at $H=(18,12-6\sqrt3+4\sqrt3)=(18,12-2\sqrt3)$. So $EH=\frac{12}{\cos30^\circ}=8\sqrt3$ and $[AEH]=\frac12\cdot12\cdot8\sqrt3=48\sqrt3$. Right $\triangle ADH$: $AD=18$, $DH=2\sqrt3$, area $18\sqrt3$. So $[AEHD]=66\sqrt3$ and the shaded total is $2(216-66\sqrt3)\approx203.37$.

**Answer: (C) 203.4**

cemc-cayley-2007-24.title: Use as few 1s as possible
cemc-cayley-2007-24.body:
Choose integers greater than $1$ with product $2007$, then pad with $1$s to make the sum $2007$. To minimize $n$, the non-1 part should have the largest possible sum.

$2007=3^2\times223$ ($223$ is prime). Ways to write it with factors $>1$ (more than one factor, since $n>1$ and a single $2007$ would need no $1$s): $\{3,669\}$ (sum $672$), $\{9,223\}$ (sum $232$), $\{3,3,223\}$ (sum $229$). Using $\{3,669\}$ we need $2007-672=1335$ ones, so $n=1335+2=1337$.

**Answer: (B) 1337**

cemc-cayley-2007-25.title: A lies on a semicircle
cemc-cayley-2007-25.body:
Since $\angle WAX=90^\circ$ always, $A$ lies on the semicircle with diameter $WX$. Put $P=(6,0)$ and the big square's bottom-left corner at $(0,0)$; then $W=(2,4)$, $X=(4,4)$, so the centre is $M=(3,4)$ and the radius is $1$. $PM=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5$. So $AP\le AM+MP=1+5=6$, with equality when $A$ is on line $PM$ beyond $M$ (that point is on the upper semicircle, so it is allowed).

**Answer: (E) 6.0**
